```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, dpi = 300)
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(knitr)

r1 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 1)
r2 <- function(x) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = 2)
fmt_p <- function(p) {
  if (p < .001) "< .001" else paste0("= ", sub("^0", "", sprintf("%.3f", p)))
}
coef_row <- function(model, x) tidy(model, conf.int = TRUE) %>% filter(term == x)

days <- read_csv("day.csv") %>%
  mutate(temp.in.C = -8 + (39 - (-8)) * temp,
         windspeed.in.mph = windspeed * 67,
         month = factor(mnth, levels = 1:12, labels = month.abb))

cors <- cor(select(days, cnt, temp.in.C, windspeed.in.mph))

m.cnt.by.windspeed <- lm(cnt ~ windspeed.in.mph, data = days)
m.cnt.by.temp <- lm(cnt ~ temp.in.C, data = days)
m.cnt.by.windspeed.temp <- lm(cnt ~ windspeed.in.mph + temp.in.C, data = days)
models <- list(`Wind speed only` = m.cnt.by.windspeed,
               `Temperature only` = m.cnt.by.temp,
               `Wind speed and temperature` = m.cnt.by.windspeed.temp)
r.sq <- map_dbl(models, ~ summary(.x)$r.squared)

w1 <- coef_row(m.cnt.by.windspeed, "windspeed.in.mph")
t1 <- coef_row(m.cnt.by.temp, "temp.in.C")
w2 <- coef_row(m.cnt.by.windspeed.temp, "windspeed.in.mph")
t2 <- coef_row(m.cnt.by.windspeed.temp, "temp.in.C")
df1 <- df.residual(m.cnt.by.temp)
df2 <- df.residual(m.cnt.by.windspeed.temp)

m.temp.by.windspeed <- lm(temp.in.C ~ windspeed.in.mph, data = days)
cold.per.mph <- -coef(m.temp.by.windspeed)["windspeed.in.mph"]

m.cnt.by.temp.month <- lm(cnt ~ temp.in.C * month, data = days)
interaction.test <- anova(m.cnt.by.temp.month)["temp.in.C:month", ]

m.slopes <- lm(cnt ~ 0 + month + month:temp.in.C, data = days)
month.slopes <- tidy(m.slopes, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  filter(str_detect(term, ":temp.in.C")) %>%
  mutate(month = str_remove_all(term, "month|:temp.in.C"))
slope <- function(m) month.slopes %>% filter(month == m)
ci_text <- function(row) paste0("[", r1(row$conf.low), ", ", r1(row$conf.high), "]")
# CI for a negative coefficient reported as "fewer" rentals
ci_fewer <- function(row) paste0("[", r1(-row$conf.high), ", ", r1(-row$conf.low), "]")

year.means <- days %>% group_by(yr) %>% summarise(mean.cnt = mean(cnt))
```

## Method

The data were the `r nrow(days)` days of the Capital Bikeshare daily data from the UCI Machine Learning Repository, covering 1 January 2011 to 31 December 2012. The outcome was the total number of bikes rented each day. Temperature and wind speed were converted back from their normalised values to degrees Celsius and miles per hour. I fitted three linear regressions predicting daily rentals from wind speed, from temperature, and from both together. To see whether the effect of temperature changes over the year, I added a temperature × month interaction. All analyses were run in R.

## Results

On average `r format(round(mean(days$cnt)), big.mark = ",")` bikes were rented per day (*SD* = `r format(round(sd(days$cnt)), big.mark = ",")`). The mean temperature was `r r1(mean(days$temp.in.C))` °C (*SD* = `r r1(sd(days$temp.in.C))`) and the mean wind speed was `r r1(mean(days$windspeed.in.mph))` mph (*SD* = `r r1(sd(days$windspeed.in.mph))`). Rentals were positively correlated with temperature, *r* = `r r2(cors["cnt", "temp.in.C"])`, and negatively correlated with wind speed, *r* = `r r2(cors["cnt", "windspeed.in.mph"])`. Temperature and wind speed were only weakly correlated, *r* = `r r2(cors["temp.in.C", "windspeed.in.mph"])`, so collinearity was not a problem when both were entered together. The regression results are in Table 1.

```{r table-1}
coef.table <- map_dfr(models, ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE), .id = "model") %>%
  mutate(cell = paste0(r1(estimate), " [", r1(conf.low), ", ", r1(conf.high), "]"),
         term = recode(term, `(Intercept)` = "Intercept",
                       windspeed.in.mph = "Wind speed (mph)",
                       temp.in.C = "Temperature (°C)")) %>%
  select(model, term, cell) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = cell, values_fill = "")

fit.table <- tibble(term = "R²", !!!map(models, ~ r2(summary(.x)$r.squared)))

table.1 <- bind_rows(coef.table, fit.table) %>% rename(` ` = term)
kable(table.1, caption = "Table 1. Regressions of daily bike rentals on wind speed and temperature. Cells show unstandardised coefficients with 95% confidence intervals.")
```

On their own, each degree Celsius of temperature was associated with `r r1(t1$estimate)` more rentals per day, 95% CI `r ci_text(t1)`, *t*(`r df1`) = `r r2(t1$statistic)`, *p* `r fmt_p(t1$p.value)`, and each mile per hour of wind speed with `r r1(-w1$estimate)` fewer rentals, 95% CI `r ci_fewer(w1)`, *t*(`r df1`) = `r r2(w1$statistic)`, *p* `r fmt_p(w1$p.value)`. In the multiple regression, holding wind speed constant, each degree Celsius was associated with `r r1(t2$estimate)` more rentals, 95% CI `r ci_text(t2)`, *t*(`r df2`) = `r r2(t2$statistic)`, *p* `r fmt_p(t2$p.value)`. Holding temperature constant, each mile per hour of wind was associated with `r r1(-w2$estimate)` fewer rentals, 95% CI `r ci_fewer(w2)`, *t*(`r df2`) = `r r2(w2$statistic)`, *p* `r fmt_p(w2$p.value)`.

The wind speed estimate was smaller once temperature was controlled for. This is because windier days were also colder days (each extra mile per hour went with `r r2(cold.per.mph)` °C lower temperature), so in the wind speed only model part of the effect of temperature was attributed to wind. The temperature estimate changed very little. Temperature was also by far the better predictor. It explained `r r1(100 * r.sq[["Temperature only"]])`% of the variance in daily rentals on its own, compared with `r r1(100 * r.sq[["Wind speed only"]])`% for wind speed, and adding wind speed to temperature increased *R*² by only `r r1(100 * (r.sq[["Wind speed and temperature"]] - r.sq[["Temperature only"]]))` percentage points. If only one of the two could be known, temperature would be the more useful.

The relationship between temperature and rentals differed across months (Figure 1), *F*(`r interaction.test$Df`, `r df.residual(m.cnt.by.temp.month)`) = `r r2(interaction.test[["F value"]])`, *p* `r fmt_p(interaction.test[["Pr(>F)"]])` for the temperature × month interaction. In the cooler months from October to May, apart from November, warmer days had more rentals, with the steepest slope in March (`r r1(slope("Mar")$estimate)` bikes per °C, 95% CI `r ci_text(slope("Mar"))`). In June and July the slope was negative (June: `r r1(slope("Jun")$estimate)`, 95% CI `r ci_text(slope("Jun"))`; July: `r r1(slope("Jul")$estimate)`, 95% CI `r ci_text(slope("Jul"))`), meaning that on days that were already hot, higher temperatures went with fewer rentals. The slopes for August, September and November were not significantly different from zero.

```{r figure-1, fig.cap="Figure 1. Daily bike rentals against temperature, by month. Lines are linear fits with 95% confidence bands."}
ggplot(days, aes(x = temp.in.C, y = cnt)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 0.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  facet_wrap(~ month) +
  labs(x = "Temperature (°C)", y = "Number of bikes rented")
```

## Discussion

More bikes were rented on warmer days and fewer on windy days, but temperature mattered much more than wind. The temperature effect was positive in the cooler part of the year and negative in June and July. These are observational data, so the estimates are associations. The models also leave out other variables that affect rentals, such as rain, humidity, working days and the growth in use between years (an average of `r format(round(year.means$mean.cnt[year.means$yr == 0]), big.mark = ",")` rentals per day in 2011 against `r format(round(year.means$mean.cnt[year.means$yr == 1]), big.mark = ",")` in 2012).
